sections.h2: Choosing a sale route in Longview
sections.html:
An owner in a hurry can list with an agent, sell privately or take a cash offer that leaves repairs to the buyer. A listing reaches the most buyers. A cash sale closes sooner when repairs, liens, tenants or an estate stand in the way.

Longview is the seat of Gregg County, along Interstate 20 and U.S. highways 80 and 259, roughly 125 miles east of Dallas. The city also reaches across the line into Harrison County, so your parcel's county decides which appraisal district and which clerk handle your paperwork. Much of the housing dates from a mid-century boom, and buyers inspecting those homes focus on roofs, foundations, old wiring and plumbing. Expect repair requests on an older Longview house.

  • Confirm the county from your deed or tax bill before you request offers.
  • Collect the deed, any mortgage payoff statement and the latest tax bill.
  • Set any cash offer beside the likely proceeds of a listing, minus repairs, commission and months of upkeep.

The Gregg County Appraisal District values real and business personal property in that county under the Texas Property Tax Code. Parcels on the Harrison side belong to that county's appraisal district, so check your tax statement for the office that applies. The clerk of that same county records your deed.

Gregg's district is running a residential reappraisal through March 2027, with exterior inspections and new photographs. Appraisers carry a pictured ID, a business card and a state registration card, and they leave a door hanger and card when no one is home.

The Gregg district lists three conditions for a homestead exemption: you hold title and use the home as your residence on the filing date, no spouse claims a residence homestead elsewhere, and you present a Texas license or state ID showing the same address. Its taxpayer liaison is at 4367 W Loop 281 in Longview, and the number is 903-238-8823.

Heirs missing from a recorded deed can submit an ownership affidavit to the district to claim the exemption.

  • School districts exempt $140,000 of a homestead's value, with a further $60,000 for seniors and disabled owners.
  • A disabled veteran receives a tiered partial exemption, and a 100 percent rating can mean a total exemption on the homestead.

At a sale, the title company divides the year's bill between buyer and seller. An open lien gets a payoff request and is cleared from your proceeds.

Call the lender or the tax office before a deadline, since both processes move in fixed steps. A Texas deed of trust lets a lender sell without a court, but only after a default notice with a twenty-day cure period and a sale notice three weeks ahead of an auction held early in a month.

Afterward, a lender may sue for a shortfall within two years. Redemption after a tax sale is narrow: two years for homestead, farm or mineral property and 180 days for other land.

Closing a sale before the auction often leaves an owner better off than the auction price would. Have the payoff amounts and lien balances put in writing by the title company.

Begin with the deed. If the owner has passed away, work out whether probate is needed: a will can be probated for four years after death, and a muniment of title can pass real estate where the estate owes nothing beyond real-estate liens.

For a rented house, expect three days' written notice, a justice court filing, service on the tenant four days ahead of trial and a writ of possession six days after judgment. Because of that schedule, many owners sell while the renter is still living there.

The clerk of Gregg or Harrison County keeps the records, depending on where the land lies. The signature needs a notary's acknowledgment, and the clerk can quote current charges. Closing funds usually cover them. Check that the legal description matches the deed already of record.

sections.h2: Documents and calls to make first
sections.html:
Gather the deed, your latest tax bill and any loan payoff statement. Call the appraisal district named on that bill and ask which exemptions are active. Ask the tax office for the amount owed today and on your hoped-for closing date. If an old lien turns up in the county records, tell the title company at once; it is easier to clear one before a contract than after.

If you rent the house out, collect the lease and tell any buyer about it in writing.

1. Collect offers from a cash buyer and, if you want, a listing agent.
  2. Compare the amount each leaves you after payoffs, tax share and repair costs.
  3. Open title with a title company and give it your payoff figures.
  4. Sign the deed before a notary.
  5. Funds are released and the deed is filed with the county clerk.

A cash purchase generally skips the lender's appraisal, so closing can come quickly once title is clear.

faqs.q: Is a Longview house in Gregg or Harrison County?
faqs.a: Either, because the city crosses the county line. The appraisal district on your tax bill is the office to contact, and the clerk of that same county records the deed.

faqs.q: Can a lien stop a Longview sale?
faqs.a: No, though it must be paid. The title company requests payoff figures and settles liens from your proceeds, and a buyer cannot receive clear title while delinquent property taxes remain.

faqs.q: When are Longview property taxes late?
faqs.a: Most unpaid bills turn delinquent on February 1. A six percent penalty and one percent interest apply then, and the penalty grows monthly until July 1.

faqs.q: Must I repair a Longview house before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No. A cash buyer purchases as-is, with the price reflecting the work expected. Compare the offer against a repaired-and-listed price before deciding.

faqs.q: How quickly can foreclosure move in Texas?
faqs.a: Fast. A default notice gives twenty days to cure, a sale notice must come three weeks before the auction, and sales happen monthly. Talk to the lender early.
